mappings.note: Names the three Panchayati Raj tiers and what each does - the functioning of rural local government bodies, which is LO-246. Not LO-245, whose levels are local, state and union rather than the tiers inside local government.
A letter to the Sarpanch about roadside plastic: the pupil must know what the local government is for (LO-244) and that sanitation is the Gram Panchayat's business (LO-246).
What kind of person should sit on a Gram Panchayat - a judgement about the local government's role and who can discharge it, so LO-244.
A dangerous highway crossing outside a village school and which Panchayati Raj institutions can act: the working of rural local bodies, squarely LO-246.
Reserved seats for disadvantaged sections aiming at social justice: a measure against inequality (LO-243) built into the rural local body (LO-246).
Vandana Bahadur Maida's Bhil community - the answer is a community (LO-241), reached through her office as Sarpanch (LO-246).
The Patwari keeping land records for the Gram Panchayat; an official of the rural local administration, so LO-246.
Gram Panchayat's village remit against the Zila Parishad's district one - a contrast inside the rural local government system, so LO-246 rather than LO-245.
Identifies the Panchayat Samiti as the intermediate tier among Gram Sabha, Sarpanch and Zila Parishad; a structure item within local government, so LO-246.
What the Arthashastra does and does not cover: the contents of an ancient literary work (LO-236) on statecraft and administration (LO-244).
Panchayati Raj as self-government empowering villagers - the role of government at the local level, which LO-244 names outright.
The Sarpanch or Pradhan as the elected head of the Gram Panchayat; an office within the rural local body, so LO-246.
Dnyaneshwar Kamble as a transgender Sarpanch: the answer names an under-represented community (LO-241) holding office in a rural local body (LO-246).
Maida's work on education and sanitation - LO-246 names exactly these sectors as the business of rural local bodies.
Popatrao Pawar remaking Hiware Bazar through rainwater harvesting; a Sarpanch's development work, so LO-246.
The Panchayat Secretary calling meetings and keeping records - an administrative office of the rural local body, hence LO-246.
The Patwari as the village revenue official keeping land records and maps; mapped with the other Patwari item under LO-246.
The Child-Friendly Panchayat Initiative giving children a voice through Bal Sabhas: a programme of the rural local body (LO-246) extending democratic participation (CG-SST3).
Almost two-thirds of India living in villages - the scale that makes rural local government necessary, so LO-244.
The difficulty of meeting varied local needs across a vast country; the argument for government at the local level, hence LO-244.
Names 'Panchayat' as the village council - the basic term for the rural local body, so LO-246.
How Panchayats bring governance within reach by enabling participation: the local government's role (LO-244) as a democratic process (CG-SST3).
Panchayati Raj classed as self-government rather than monarchy or colonial rule - the nature of the local government's role, so LO-244.
The Gram Panchayat as the base of the three tiers; a structure item inside rural local government, hence LO-246.
The Gram Sabha as all enrolled adult voters of the village: an organ of the rural local body (LO-246) and the most direct form of democracy in the chapter (CG-SST3).
One-third of Panchayat seats reserved for women - a measure against gender inequality (LO-243) inside the rural local body (LO-246).
Kautilya as the author of the Arthashastra; authorship of an ancient literary work, so LO-236 alone.
The sangrahana serving ten villages in the Arthashastra: content of the ancient text (LO-236) describing a unit of local administration (LO-244).
Kautilya's ladder from village clusters to provincial headquarters read as an early tiered governance system - the text (LO-236) and the administrative idea (LO-244).
Panchayati Raj as a three-tier system; a structure item within rural local government, so LO-246.
Panchayati Raj letting villagers plan their own development: the local government's role (LO-244) through participatory democracy (CG-SST3).
Finds Popatrao Pawar wrongly credited with industrial pollution control among Kamble, Maida and Kautilya; the item turns on what each Sarpanch actually did, so LO-246.

A damaged duplicate whose supplied answer is about Panchayati Raj being three-tier, one-third of seats reserved for women and members being elected: the structure of the rural body (LO-246) and the reservation for women (LO-243).
A falling village well referred to the Gram Sabha and Panchayat rather than a court or national commission - which local body handles what, so LO-246.
Kamble's motto 'lok seva, gram seva' equating service to the village with service to the public; an idea about what local government is for, so LO-244.
Panchayati Raj varying between States because local government is a state subject: the rural bodies themselves (LO-246) and the relation between the state and local levels (LO-245).
Anna Hazare's watershed model aimed at conserving water, as applied in Hiware Bazar - a development programme run through the rural local body, so LO-246.
The karvatika over a hundred villages in the Arthashastra; the ancient text (LO-236) on administrative units (LO-244), like the sangrahana item.
Bal Panchayats drawing children into democratic practice: an initiative of the rural local body (LO-246) teaching democratic participation (CG-SST3).

A damaged duplicate whose supplied answer is that old land-record maps show how land was once owned and divided: records used as historical evidence (LO-234), kept by the village revenue office (LO-246).
